briefing.text: The hypothesis makes a functional claim: that ARAF N217I and G322S ACTIVATE the pathway. Before you choose a label, list every provided file and its columns, and check whether any variable measures pathway (MAPK/ERK) activity directly, such as mRNA expression, protein or phospho-protein, RPPA or a signature score. The files described are clinical patient/sample, gene panel matrix, mutations and SVs. If none of them measures activity, say in your reasoning how you dealt with that gap.
briefing.reason: Whether a measured outcome variable exists decides which label is possible. Teams need to check this directly, not assume it.

briefing.text: Finding ARAF p.N217I and p.G322S in data_mutations.txt shows only that the variants are present. It does not show what they do. Pull the ARAF rows and record sample IDs, HGVSp_Short, Variant_Classification and VAF (t_alt_count/t_depth). Keep 'the mutation exists' separate from 'the mutation activates the pathway' in your reasoning.
briefing.reason: The most likely mistake is to treat the presence of the variants as support for activation.

briefing.text: Under the task's label definitions, 'False' needs evidence in the data that goes against activation, for example a measured variable showing the pathway is not activated in ARAF-mutant tumours. Missing supporting data is not contradiction. Ask whether any variable could actually show non-activation before you consider 'False'.
briefing.reason: This stops teams from mixing up 'cannot be shown' with 'contradicted', which is a key distinction in the labels.

briefing.text: If you use mutual exclusivity of ARAF mutations with KRAS G12/G13/Q61, BRAF V600 or NRAS hotspots as indirect evidence of a MAPK driver role, count the overlap at sample level. Check how many samples the cohort has, because a small cohort gives almost no statistical power. Exclusivity is weak, suggestive evidence. On its own it can neither confirm nor refute activation.
briefing.reason: This is the only plausible indirect test in mutation-only data. Teams need to know its limits so they do not over-read it in either direction. The library's sample count was approximate, so I left it out and ask teams to count themselves.

briefing.text: N217 sits in the ARAF CR2 regulatory region next to the known activating S214 site. G322 lies outside that region. The two variants may therefore not behave the same, so assess them separately. Any argument by analogy, such as 'N217 resembles S214', is prior knowledge, not evidence from this data. Label it that way.
briefing.reason: The hypothesis names two variants. Treating them as one, or passing off literature analogy as data evidence, would distort the conclusion.

briefing.text: Run basic QC on the ARAF calls. Check dbSNP_RS, allele counts and VAF, and whether the same coordinate recurs suspiciously across samples. ARAF is on chrX, so interpret VAF in light of each patient's sex. Calls that look germline or artefactual weaken any driver interpretation.
briefing.reason: This shows whether the variants are credible somatic events. That matters for any indirect argument.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assumed 'the pathway' means the MAPK/ERK pathway. The hypothesis never names it, and neither team checked whether any variable in the data refers to a named pathway.

Both teams assumed that a variant being present and not co-occurring with other drivers counts as support for 'activation'. That turns a functional claim into a claim about presence. Neither team asked whether the same pattern would be expected if the variants were passengers. With 8 samples, 2 carriers, and few other MAPK drivers in the cohort, exclusivity is nearly guaranteed by chance.

Both teams built their exclusivity test from a hand-picked list of genes (RAS/RAF/MEK/selected RTKs/FGFR/IDH). Neither team tested whether the list was complete. Other RTK and RAS-regulator genes that are mutated or fused in the ARAF-mutant samples may have been left out.
Both teams treated the ARAF calls as somatic and real, although no allele counts, normal counts or Mutation_Status values are available.
unused_evidence: The Hotspot column in data_mutations.txt (0/FAILED for every row). It is 0 for both ARAF rows. This is the data's own annotation of whether a variant is a recognised recurrent hotspot. Neither team reported it, and it bears directly on whether calling these variants activating is supported by anything in the data.

Annotation_Status (6 FAILED rows), and the empty Mutation_Status/Validation_Status/Verification_Status/n_ref/n_alt columns. Together these show the somatic status of the ARAF calls cannot be confirmed from the file.

data_sv.txt RNA_support=Yes / DNA_support=No for every fusion. RNA was sequenced, yet no expression table was provided. The SV table also includes RIN1 fusions (a RAS effector) in several samples, one of them the G322S carrier. Neither team's gene list for exclusivity covered RIN1, EPHA2/EPHA3 or PREX2. All of these are mutated or fused in an ARAF-mutant sample.

TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS in data_clinical_sample.txt. The ARAF-mutant samples are among the lowest-TMB tumours. Neither team used this to judge whether two isolated missense variants are more likely drivers or passengers.
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams named the same weak point: the claim is functional and the data contain no activity readout. Neither resolved it. Both reported it and chose True anyway, with confidence 0.50-0.55. Team B said explicitly that the evidence 'could equally justify Not verifiable'. Team A's argument that 'no variable could show non-activation, so False is not chosen' is equally an argument that no variable can show activation.
Team A noted that germline status cannot be checked (chrX, no sex, no VAF) but did not say how this uncertainty affects the label.
Neither team showed that its exclusivity observation has any power: no null expectation, no permutation, no count of how many samples carry any MAPK driver at all.
second_readings: 'lead to activation of the pathway' can be read as a causal/functional claim (variant → measured pathway activity). On that reading the data, which have no expression, protein or signature table, hold no relevant outcome variable. That is the task's own definition of Not verifiable.
'the pathway' is unspecified. It could mean MAPK, but it could also be any pathway the source study had in mind. Choosing MAPK is an inference from outside the data.
'ARAF mutations, specifically N217I and G322S' could be read as a claim about each variant separately. Each occurs in one sample, so any per-variant statement rests on n=1.
challenge.verdict: Low trust. Both teams labelled True with confidence of only 0.50-0.55, and both admitted that the outcome the hypothesis is about (pathway activation) has no variable in the data. The True label rests on presence plus exclusivity in 2 of 8 samples. The teams also built the exclusivity test from an incomplete gene list and ignored the data's Hotspot=0 annotation, so the agreement looks like a shared reading of the label rules rather than evidence.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Tabulate the Hotspot and Annotation_Status columns of data_mutations.txt for the two ARAF rows and for all rows. Does the data's own hotspot annotation for these variants change whether presence can be read as evidence of activation?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Count how many of the 8 samples carry any alteration in your MAPK driver list, then compute the probability that 2 randomly chosen samples would be free of all of them. If that probability is high, does mutual exclusivity still carry weight as support for True rather than Not verifiable?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: List every gene mutated or fused in ICC12 and ICC18, including the RNA-supported fusions in data_sv.txt (e.g. RIN1) and RTK/RAS-regulator genes such as EPHA2, EPHA3 and PREX2. Do any of them fall in the signalling pathway you assumed, and does that change your exclusivity finding?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Read the hypothesis's phrase 'lead to activation of the pathway' against the task's definition of Not verifiable. Name the single column in the data that measures the outcome (activation). If there is none, explain why the label is not governed by that definition.

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your plan said: 'If only mutation calls exist, activation is untestable -> Not verifiable'. You found only mutation calls and SVs, yet you labelled True. Re-check whether any file holds an activity readout. If none does, what in the data justified departing from your own pre-stated rule?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Tabulate the Hotspot column of data_mutations.txt for the ARAF N217I and G322S rows. Does the data's own annotation that these are not hotspots alter the weight you give to their presence?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your co-occurrence gene list omitted EPHA2, EPHA3, PREX2 and the RAS effector RIN1, which appear as mutations or RNA-supported fusions in data_sv.txt and data_mutations.txt. Re-run the co-occurrence check with every alteration present in ICC12 and ICC18. Does 'no co-occurring driver' still hold?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Empty t_alt_count/n_alt_count/Mutation_Status columns mean the somatic status of the chrX ARAF calls cannot be confirmed. Check these columns and Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode for the ARAF rows. Does an unconfirmable somatic status change your label?

referee.difference: Same data facts on both sides (ARAF G322S in ICC12, N217I in ICC18, no activity readout). They differ only in how they read the task: X says the outcome variable (pathway activation) is missing, so the answer is Not verifiable. Y says the mutation variables count as 'relevant variables' and nothing contradicts the claim, so the answer is True.
referee.test: test.py checks every non-empty column in all 5 files for a variable that measures activation or could stand in for it (expression, phospho, RPPA, score, signature). It also gives the one usable data proxy for driver/activating status: the chance that the 2 ARAF-mutant samples would both lack other MAPK drivers anyway. If 'True' is to rest on data, the data need either a column measuring activation that is higher in the ARAF mutants, or exclusivity that is unlikely by chance.
referee.expected_if_x: No column measures activation, and the exclusivity proxy is uninformative (chance probability high). Then nothing in the data analysis supports 'leads to activation', and the Not verifiable definition (outcome variable absent) applies.
referee.expected_if_y: Some column measures activation and is higher in ICC12/ICC18, or the exclusivity with other MAPK drivers is unlikely by chance, so the analysis supports the claim.
referee.outcome: The non-empty columns are clinical identifiers, ONCOTREE, TMB, mutation annotation (the Score and allele-count columns are entirely empty, and Hotspot is 0 for every annotated row) and SV fusion/support flags. None measures pathway activation. Only ICC24 (FGFR2-PPHLN1) carries a canonical MAPK driver, so P(both ARAF samples driver-free by chance) = C(7,2)/C(8,2) = 0.75, which is uninformative.
referee.reason: 'True' needs the analysis to support the hypothesis. Y's support is only that the mutations are present, which is the hypothesis's premise, not evidence for its claim of activation. The test found neither a variable measuring activation nor an informative proxy, so the claim's outcome cannot be assessed from these data. That matches X's Not verifiable. Caveat: if the grader treats the presence of the named variants as verification, Y's label would match instead.

questions.question: In MAF files exported for cBioPortal, how is the 'Hotspot' column defined (which hotspot resource and which criteria), and what does a value of 0 mean versus a missing value?
questions.why: Neither team used this column. Whether 0 means 'checked and not a recurrent hotspot' or merely 'not annotated' decides whether it is evidence about the variants' functional status.

questions.question: How much statistical evidence can mutual exclusivity between a candidate driver and known pathway drivers provide in very small cohorts (fewer than 10 samples), and what null model is standard for testing it?
questions.why: Both teams' True label rests on exclusivity in a tiny cohort. Its evidential value under a proper null decides whether True or Not verifiable is defensible.

questions.question: In cBioPortal structural-variant files, what does RNA_support=Yes with DNA_support=No indicate about the sequencing assays performed, and does it imply that expression data were generated but not provided?
questions.why: This bears on whether the absence of an activity readout is a feature of the study or of the provided tables, and so on whether the claim is testable at all.

findings.question: In MAF files exported for cBioPortal, how is the 'Hotspot' column defined (which hotspot resource and which criteria), and what does a value of 0 mean versus a missing value?
findings.answer: NOT SETTLED BY THE WEB: all research-gateway calls (2 searches, 2 contents fetches) failed with HTTP 502 / Exa 403, so no page was read. Unverified prior knowledge only: 'Hotspot' is not a standard column of the cBioPortal MAF specification. cBioPortal annotates hotspots itself at display time, using cancerhotspots.org (Chang et al. 2016/2018, statistically recurrent single-residue and in-frame-indel hotspots). A Hotspot 0/1 column in a study MAF is a pipeline-specific flag; 0 most likely means 'not matched to a known hotspot', which does not show the variant is non-functional, and a missing value means not annotated. Do not use Hotspot=0 as evidence against activation without documentation.

findings.question: In cBioPortal structural-variant files, what does RNA_support=Yes with DNA_support=No indicate about the sequencing assays performed, and does it imply that expression data were generated but not provided?
findings.answer: NOT SETTLED BY THE WEB: the gateway failed, so no page was read. Unverified prior knowledge only: in the cBioPortal SV format, DNA_Support and RNA_Support are optional Yes/No fields that say whether the event was detected in DNA or in RNA sequence data. RNA_Support=Yes means some RNA-based assay (RNA-seq or a targeted RNA fusion panel) was run on that sample. DNA_Support=No may mean 'not detected' or 'not assessed in DNA'. Neither field shows that genome-wide expression data were generated or withheld. Whatever else the study did, the provided tables contain no expression or pathway-activity readout.
